name: Copy.ai
subcategory: AI drafting, research and content optimization
tagline: Build repeatable go-to-market drafting workflows from approved company context

pricing.notes: Typical self-serve paid tier; plan names and included workflow credits can change.

tiers.name: Chat
tiers.limits: 5 seats; unlimited chat words and projects.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats and credits; unlimited workflows; 20+ integrations; API access.

pricing.billingTerms: Chat is monthly + annual; automation plans are annual-only; Enterprise is custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Workflow credit consumption varies by workflow and model. Additional credits cost extra; upgrades are prorated and downgrades are handled as account credit.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Copy.ai, build repeatable go-to-market drafting workflows from approved company context. The hard boundary is workflow templates, account data, team collaboration, and model routing, plus workflow, data, and model tuning.
coreLoopDIY: Take a brief, gather approved company context and source material, generate structured go-to-market drafts in repeatable workflows, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
whatYouLose: workflow templates, account data, team collaboration, and model routing
ongoingBurden: prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Copy.ai because the subscription bundles a refined workflow, proprietary signals, templates, and predictable output quality for a team. The recurring cost buys prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Active open-source interface for local and API-backed language models with retrieval features.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local-first AI desk with reusable agents, documents, memory, and workflows; less campaign theatre, more settings.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can build reusable agents over company context, but it lacks Copy.ai's managed go-to-market workflow library, integrations, approvals, and team governance.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Jan
alternatives.desc: A desktop ChatGPT-shaped box with local models and reusable assistants; excellent at prompts, blissfully unaware of your marketing calendar.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Built-in local inference via llama.cpp/llama-server plus OpenAI-compatible APIs and connectors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Threads, assistants, settings and downloaded model files live in Jan's local data folder; only requests sent to configured cloud providers leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: Its reusable assistants are prompt-driven rather than a managed GTM workflow system with connected sales and marketing data.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires downloading a multi-gigabyte model and enough RAM; cloud use requires an API key

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted AI workbench with saved prompts, knowledge, web search, and multi-model comparison; powerful, not especially house-trained.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It can host prompts, knowledge, and tools, but it does not provide Copy.ai's packaged GTM processes, integration catalog, or operational governance.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Chat plan and a personal content workstation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Copy.ai in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: take a brief, gather approved company context and source material, generate structured go-to-market drafts in repeatable workflows, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a brief form with audience, objective, tone, source URLs, and prohibited claims.
Store imported source text locally and chunk it for retrieval with SQLite FTS5.
Generate an outline first and require approval before drafting sections.
Attach source references to generated paragraphs and flag unsupported claims.
Provide rewrite controls for shorten, clarify, change tone, and add evidence.
Export clean Markdown plus a JSON research bundle.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live search-engine rank data.
Deliberately leave out automatic publishing to third-party CMSs.
Deliberately leave out multi-user approvals and brand governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
